title: India Tour of New Zealand: Full Commentators List and How to Watch
excerpt: Shastri, Gavaskar, Bhogle, Smith and Doull headline the panels as Sony carries the tour in India and Sky Sport brings a first full-tour Hindi feed in New Zealand.
body:
• India's tour of New Zealand runs October 22 to December 1, 2026: five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests, opening with a T20I at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, at 12:30 p.m. IST.
  • In India, watch on Sony Sports Network and SonyLIV; in New Zealand, Sky Sport and Sky Sport Now carry the tour live and on demand.
  • Sky's English panel for the white-ball matches: Ian Smith, Ravi Shastri, Stephen Fleming (T20Is only), Simon Doull, Katey Martin, Ross Taylor, Tim Southee, Scott Styris and Shane Bond; Sunil Gavaskar and Harsha Bhogle join for the Tests.
  • Sky offers Hindi commentary for an entire tour for the first time, on Sky Sport Select, in partnership with Sony Pictures Networks India — Shastri, Gavaskar and Bhogle form the Hindi world feed.

India's six-week tour of New Zealand comes with one of the largest broadcast teams assembled for a bilateral series, as Sony Sports Network in India and Sky Sport in New Zealand confirmed their commentary panels for five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests from October 22 to December 1.

In India the matches are on Sony Sports Network and SonyLIV. In New Zealand, Sky has won the home rights back from TVNZ, with coverage live and on demand on Sky Sport and Sky Sport Now, according to CricExec's report of Sky's announcement. The tour marks 100 years of sporting ties between the two countries, and Hero VIDA is title sponsor across all 12 matches.

Who is on the microphone

Sony's Extraaa Innings studio panel has 10 names: Ravi Shastri, Sunil Gavaskar, Ajinkya Rahane, Ravichandran Ashwin, Shardul Thakur, Ajay Jadeja, Venkatesh Prasad, Ian Smith, Simon Doull and Harsha Bhogle.

Sky's English team splits by format. For the T20Is and ODIs it is Ian Smith, Ravi Shastri, Stephen Fleming (T20Is only), Simon Doull, Katey Martin, Ross Taylor, Tim Southee, Scott Styris and Shane Bond. For the Tests it is Smith, Doull, Gavaskar, Katey Martin, Bhogle and Styris. Laura McGoldrick presents Sky's coverage. Shastri leads the white-ball matches and Gavaskar leads the Tests.

"It's great to be back behind the microphone for Sky. You could hardly ask for a bigger stage to begin with than India."

— Ian Smith, Sky commentator

Hindi commentary for a full tour, a first for Sky

Sky is offering Hindi commentary across the whole tour for the first time, in partnership with Sony Pictures Networks India, with the feed on Sky Sport Select through the T20I, ODI and Test series. Shastri, Gavaskar and Bhogle also contribute to Sky's world feed. Sony's Rajesh Kaul said New Zealand's large and growing Indian community made a full-tour Hindi feed important so fans could follow the series "in a language that brings them closer to the action."

Sky is also upgrading production for the tour, with a Raptor Cam aerial system, Virtual Eye tracking and 3D graphics, and a 26-camera set-up.

Dates and start times to plan around

The T20Is run October 22 to November 1, the ODIs November 4 to 15, and the Tests start November 19 in Wellington and November 27 in Christchurch, ending December 1. Start times in India are friendly for the white-ball games and brutal for the Tests: T20Is begin at 12:30 p.m. IST, ODIs at 7:30 a.m. IST, and Tests at 3:30 a.m. IST. Venues are Hagley Oval in Christchurch, Wellington, Eden Park in Auckland, Seddon Park in Hamilton and Bay Oval in Tauranga.

For diaspora viewers in New Zealand, Sky Sport Now is the streaming route; for viewers in India, SonyLIV. The Hindi feed on Sky Sport Select is the notable new option for families in New Zealand who have previously had English-only coverage of a home India tour.
